summary: Same pattern — a smoothly translating full-spectrum rainbow on the strip, with several palette modes, and the port reproduces three of the original's six modes essentially exactly (the HSLuv mode is byte-identical at HSLuvLightness=0.5) — but the RainbowMode index is shifted by one from mode 1 upward, the original's two constant-brightness rainbow modes are missing entirely, and the Speed dial follows a quadratic law topping out at 20 px/s instead of the original's linear 46 px/s (4.6x too slow at mid-dial).
observations: Both sides draw one continuous R->Y->G->C->B->M->R rainbow spanning the whole 60-px strip, translating toward pixel 0 (leftward), with no dark gaps, no sparkle, no events; the 60 s / 5 fps survey shows a single unchanging regime on both sides and the t=180-210 s window (steady-late) is identical in stats to t=0, so neither side decays, freezes or blows up.

Untouched defaults: original is completely frozen (motion 0 on all 120 baseline frames, 0.00 px/s measured over a 20 s dump), port drifts leftward at 1.75 px/s. So the original's internal Speed default is 0 and the port's is not.

Speed law (mode 0, 60 px, phase measured by circular cross-correlation of dumped frames over a 2 s baseline): original is LINEAR — 0.1/0.2/0.35/0.5/0.65/0.8/1.0 give -4.5/-9.0/-16.0/-23.0/-30.0/-36.5/-46.0 px/s (v = -46*s). Port is QUADRATIC and much slower — 0.0/-1.0/-2.5/-5.0/-8.5/-13.0/-20.0 px/s (v = -20*s^2). Direction is correct on both. At Speed=0.5 the port is 4.6x too slow; at Speed=1.0, 2.3x too slow; at Speed=0.1 the port is visually frozen while the original still creeps.
Neither side is frame-rate coupled: at 10/20/40 fps with Speed=0.5 both hold their velocity exactly (orig -23.0 px/s, port -5.0 px/s at all three rates).

RainbowMode index is shifted by one from index 1 up. Frozen 12-px ramp dumps: orig 0 = plain linear rainbow; orig 1 = fixed hue-stretch (178/18/0, 178/71/0, 178/156/0, ...); orig 2 = gain-controlled rainbow (responds to GainParam); orig 3 and 4 = constant-brightness rainbows; orig 5 = HSLuv. Port 0 AND port 1 are both the plain linear rainbow (identical byte-for-byte), port 2 = the fixed hue-stretch, port 3 = the gain-controlled rainbow, port 6 = HSLuv. So port mode N reproduces orig mode N-1 for N=2,3 and N=6, and a user picking mode 3 sees a different look on each side.

The original's two constant-brightness modes have no counterpart in the port. At 60 px, orig mode 3 holds its R+G+B channel sum between 178 and 275 and orig mode 4 between 177 and 238 (peaks pulled down to ~119 in the mixed hues); port modes 4 and 5 keep the sum swinging 165-330 with the peak channel pinned at 165 — they are just plain/hue-offset full-brightness rainbows. Port modes 4 and 5 are also near-duplicates of each other and respond to none of the four secondary sliders (all eight low/high sweeps byte-identical).

Non-HSLuv modes are uniformly ~7% dimmer on the port: peak channel 165 vs the original's 178 at 60 px, mean brightness 82 vs 89 across every mode-0 run. The HSLuv mode does NOT carry this offset (both mean 101 with lightness matched).

HSLuv mode is an excellent reproduction: orig mode 5 vs port mode 6 with sliderHSLuvLightness=0.5, dumped at 60 px, differ by at most 1/255 on any channel across all 180 channels (233/0/100, 236/0/73, 239/0/7, 216/64/0, ... on both). Untouched, though, the port's HSLuv mode renders brighter and less saturated (254/19/112 vs 233/0/100, mean 112 vs 101) because its internal HSLuvLightness default is above 0.5.

Out-of-range mode index behaves differently: original renders solid black for RainbowMode 6, 7, 8, 10 and 20 (mean 0, motion 0); the port clamps to its mode 6 and keeps rendering (mean 112 at every value tested).

Control surface: both sides expose 7 controls of matching kinds (1 inputNumber + 6 sliders) but FOUR names/labels differ — orig sliderGainParam/GainParam vs port sliderGainAmount/GainAmount; orig sliderGainHueToStretch/GainHueToStretch vs port sliderHueToStretch/HueToStretch; orig sliderHsluvSaturation/HsluvSaturation vs port sliderHSLuvSaturation/HSLuvSaturation; orig sliderHsluvLuminosity/HsluvLuminosity vs port sliderHSLuvLightness/HSLuvLightness.
Randomness: pattern is fully deterministic — seed 1234 renders identically to seed 1 on both sides, so no stochastic character to compare.

dials.name: inputNumberRainbowMode
dials.origEffect: Selects among 6 palette modes (0-5): 0 plain rainbow, 1 fixed hue-stretch, 2 gain-controlled hue-stretch (the only mode where GainParam bites), 3 and 4 constant-brightness rainbows, 5 HSLuv rainbow. Values >=6 render solid black.
dials.portEffect: Selects among 7 modes (0-6) with 0 and 1 duplicated: 0/1 plain rainbow, 2 fixed hue-stretch, 3 gain-controlled, 4 and 5 plain full-brightness rainbow variants (not constant-brightness), 6 HSLuv. Values >=6 clamp to mode 6 instead of blacking out. Net: correct look at the wrong index from 1 up, and the original's two constant-brightness modes are absent.

dials.name: sliderSpeed
dials.origEffect: Linear scroll speed toward pixel 0, 0 px/s at 0 up to 46 px/s at 1 (v = -46*s), fps-invariant. Internal default 0 (frozen).
dials.portEffect: Same direction and fps-invariance, but quadratic and much slower: v = -20*s^2, so 5 px/s at 0.5 and 20 px/s at 1. Internal default is non-zero (drifts at 1.75 px/s untouched).

dials.name: sliderColorShift
dials.origEffect: Rotates the rainbow's phase around the strip; 0 and 1 are identical, 0.25/0.5/0.75 shift by exactly a quarter/half/three-quarters of the strip.
dials.portEffect: Identical phase mapping at 0/0.25/0.5/0.75/1 — the dumped ramps match the original's pixel for pixel apart from the 178-vs-165 brightness scale.

dials.name: sliderGainParam / sliderGainAmount
dials.origEffect: Live only in orig mode 2: sweeping 0/0.25/0.5/0.75/1 progressively compresses the red end of the rainbow (0 = plain rainbow, 1 = 178/2/0, 178/19/0, 178/66/0, 178/158/0, ...). Inert in modes 0, 1, 3, 4 and 5 (checked at 0 and 1 in every mode).
dials.portEffect: Live only in port mode 3, with the same monotonic compression and the same ramp shape at every value (165/2/0, 165/18/0, 165/62/0, 165/147/0, ... at 1) — i.e. a faithful match of the original's gain mode, just at the shifted index and the 165 scale. Name differs (GainAmount vs GainParam), and its internal default is ~0.5 where the original's is 0.

dials.name: sliderGainHueToStretch / sliderHueToStretch
dials.origEffect: No effect on output at 0, 0.5 or 1 in any of the six modes (checked mode-by-mode with Speed pinned to 0 and RainbowMode explicitly set) — dial effect unverifiable from output.
dials.portEffect: Also inert at 0/0.5/1 in modes 2, 4 and 5. Name/label differs from the original's.

dials.name: sliderHsluvSaturation / sliderHSLuvSaturation
dials.origEffect: Inert — 0, 0.5 and 1 give byte-identical output in the HSLuv mode and in all five other modes. Dial effect unverifiable from output.
dials.portEffect: Live in port mode 6: 0 washes the whole strip to flat grey 131/131/131, 0.5 is a half-desaturated rainbow, 1 is the full HSLuv rainbow. A real control the original does not respond to.

dials.name: sliderHsluvLuminosity / sliderHSLuvLightness
dials.origEffect: Inert — 0, 0.5 and 1 give byte-identical output in every mode. Dial effect unverifiable from output.
dials.portEffect: Live in port mode 6: 0 = all black, 0.5 = exactly the original's HSLuv palette (max 1/255 channel error), 1 = all white. Untouched it sits above 0.5, so the port's default HSLuv look is brighter and less saturated than the original's.

feedback: Fix the Speed response curve first — it is the most visible error. Original: velocity is LINEAR in the dial, -46 px/s on a 60-px strip at Speed=1, -23 px/s at 0.5, -4.5 px/s at 0.1. Port: -20*s^2 px/s (-20, -5, ~0). Make the port linear and raise the full-scale rate to 46 px/s on 60 px (i.e. 0.77 strip-widths per second at full dial). Both sides are already correctly time-based and fps-invariant, so only the dial->velocity mapping needs changing.
Set the port's internal Speed default to 0. Untouched, the original is completely motionless while the port creeps at 1.75 px/s.

Drop the duplicated plain-rainbow mode so the RainbowMode index lines up. Right now port mode 1 renders the same thing as port mode 0, which pushes every later mode one index too high: the original's fixed hue-stretch is at 1 (port has it at 2), the gain-controlled mode at 2 (port: 3), and HSLuv at 5 (port: 6). The port should expose exactly 6 modes, 0-5.

Add the original's two constant-brightness rainbow modes (its modes 3 and 4). They hold the R+G+B channel sum roughly constant — around 178-275 for mode 3 and 177-238 for mode 4 on a 60-px strip — by pulling the peak channel down to ~119 in the mixed hues while pure red stays at 178, so the strip reads as even brightness all the way round instead of bright yellow/cyan/magenta bands. The port's modes 4 and 5 are currently just plain full-brightness rainbows (sum swings 165-330, peak pinned at 165) and are near-duplicates of each other.
Raise the peak channel in the non-HSLuv modes from 165 to 178 (mean brightness 82 -> 89). The HSLuv mode already has the right level; only the rainbow modes are ~7% dim.

Set the port's internal HSLuvLightness default to the value that currently corresponds to 0.5 — at that setting the port's HSLuv mode matches the original to within 1/255 on every channel, so only the default is wrong, not the palette maths.

Rename four controls to match the original exactly: GainAmount -> GainParam, HueToStretch -> GainHueToStretch, HSLuvSaturation -> HsluvSaturation, HSLuvLightness -> HsluvLuminosity (and the underlying slider identifiers likewise).
Make out-of-range RainbowMode values render black rather than clamping: the original goes fully dark for any mode index >= 6, the port keeps drawing its top mode.

The original's GainHueToStretch, HsluvSaturation and HsluvLuminosity sliders produce no visible change at 0/0.5/1 in any mode, so the port's live HSLuv saturation/lightness behaviour cannot be validated against it. Keep the controls (the surface must match) but note that a port that responds where the original does not is a difference, not an improvement, if the goal is fidelity.
experiments: ox-<mode>-<slider>-<0|1> (48 runs: every orig secondary slider at 0 and 1 in every mode 0-5)
px-<4|5>-<slider>-<0|1> (16 runs: every port secondary slider at 0 and 1 in port modes 4 and 5)
